To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a novel strategy for the construction of a novel conditionally replication competent HSV-1 vector, expressing a foreign gene, is described.
the construction of conditionally replication-competitive herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV) vectors can be accomplished in as little as 4 weeks.
the rapid construction of novel, conditionally replication-competitive HSV-1 vectors is possible using the methods described in this review.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel HSV-based gene therapies for the treatment of cancer.
the development of novel conditionally replicating HSV-1 mutant vectors as experimental therapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer.
the rapid and efficient generation of novel conditionally-replicative HSV-1 vectors for the treatment of cancer and other diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSV-1 vectors are powerful tools that can be used for the development of experimental therapeutic agents for the treatment of a variety of cancers.
the rapid and efficient methods for the construction of HSV-1 vectors are now well established.

HSV vectors can be rapidly constructed using the strategies outlined here, and that the resulting vectors are capable of efficiently expressing multiple foreign genes, and are able to replicate and kill cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these strategies can be used to rapidly construct HSV-1 vectors for use as experimental therapeutic agents in the treatment of various cancers.
we have developed a number of new strategies for the construction of conditionally replication-competitive HSV-1 vectors.

the use of the Cre-loxP system, in combination with other systems such as the FLP-FRT and the GAL4-UAS systems, can be used to generate conditionally replicating HSV-1 mutants expressing multiple genes, including reporter, therapeutic and suicide genes, in a rapid and efficient manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rapid and efficient generation of conditionally replicating HSV-1 mutants expressing foreign genes is feasible and that the strategies developed in our laboratory can be applied to the construction of other conditionally replicating vectors.
the use of a combination of strategies can significantly improve the efficiency and rapidity of HSV-1 vector construction.
HSV vectors expressing foreign genes can be generated rapidly and efficiently using various strategies, including growth selection and color selection.
